Title: Stack-based Buffer Overflow in lwm2m_write_attr_handler via Untrusted CoAP Query Options
Analysis:
- Source: Untrusted CoAP URI query options parsed from the incoming network packet and stored in `options` via `coap_find_options`.
- Sanitization/Validation: No bounds check is performed on `vlen` (the length of the parsed query option value) against the size of the destination buffer `opt_buf` (size `COAP_OPTION_BUF_LEN`, defaulting to 13 bytes).
- Sink: `memcpy(opt_buf, options[i].value + plen + 1, vlen);` copies `vlen` bytes into the stack buffer `opt_buf`, followed by `opt_buf[vlen] = '\0';` which writes a null byte out of bounds.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
  An attacker sends a CoAP PUT/POST Write Attributes request containing a query parameter like `pmin=123456789012345678901234567890` (a value of length 30).
  This results in `vlen` = 30. `memcpy` writes 30 bytes into the 13-byte stack-allocated buffer `opt_buf`, overwriting critical stack variables and the return address.

Title: Integer Underflow and Heap Buffer Overflow in JSON Format Reader get_string when buflen is 0
Analysis:
- Source: The length of the parsed string resource from the JSON payload (`fd->array_object.val_string`).
- Sanitization/Validation: The boundary check `string_length > buflen` is insufficient when `buflen` is `0` because it evaluations to `true` for any non-empty string, and subsequently calculates `string_length = buflen - 1`.
- Sink: When `buflen == 0`, `string_length = buflen - 1` wraps around to `SIZE_MAX` (due to unsigned integer underflow of `size_t`), causing `memcpy(buf, ..., SIZE_MAX)` to trigger a massive out-of-bounds copy and heap buffer overflow or crash.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
  An attacker triggers a resource write handler with `buflen == 0` (e.g. by configuring `res_inst->max_data_len` to 0 or using a user-registered `pre_write_cb` that returns 0).
  An incoming JSON payload with a string resource like `{"sv":"overflow"}` is parsed.
  Since `buflen == 0`, `string_length` underflows to `SIZE_MAX`, causing `memcpy(buf, "overflow", SIZE_MAX)` which results in stack/heap corruption and program crash.

Title: Integer Underflow and Heap Buffer Overflow in CBOR Format Reader get_string when buflen is 0
Analysis:
- Source: The length of the parsed string resource from the CBOR payload (`hndl.len`).
- Sanitization/Validation: The boundary calculation `len = MIN(buflen-1, hndl.len)` is unsafe when `buflen` is `0` because it underflows to `SIZE_MAX`.
- Sink: When `buflen == 0`, `buflen - 1` wraps around to `SIZE_MAX` (due to unsigned integer underflow of `size_t`), so `MIN(SIZE_MAX, hndl.len)` evaluates to `hndl.len`. `memcpy(value, hndl.value, len)` and `value[len] = '\0'` will copy `hndl.len` bytes to `value` out of bounds, causing a heap buffer overflow or crash.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
  An attacker triggers a resource write handler with `buflen == 0`.
  An incoming CBOR payload with a string resource of length 50 is parsed.
  Since `buflen == 0`, `len` underflows to `SIZE_MAX` inside `MIN(SIZE_MAX, 50)`, causing `memcpy(value, hndl.value, 50)` which writes 50 bytes into a 0-byte or unallocated destination buffer, followed by `value[50] = '\0'`.

Title: Integer Underflow and Heap Buffer Overflow in SenML CBOR Format Reader get_string when buflen is 0
Analysis:
- Source: The length of the parsed string resource from the SenML CBOR payload (`fd->current->record_union.union_vs.len`).
- Sanitization/Validation: The boundary calculation `len = MIN(buflen-1, fd->current->record_union.union_vs.len)` is unsafe when `buflen` is `0` because it underflows to `SIZE_MAX`.
- Sink: When `buflen == 0`, `buflen - 1` wraps around to `SIZE_MAX` (due to unsigned integer underflow of `size_t`), so `MIN(SIZE_MAX, ...)` evaluates to the incoming string length. `memcpy(buf, ..., len)` and `buf[len] = '\0'` will copy and null-terminate out of bounds, causing a heap buffer overflow or crash.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
  An attacker triggers a resource write handler with `buflen == 0`.
  An incoming SenML CBOR payload with a string resource of length 50 is parsed.
  Since `buflen == 0`, `len` underflows to `SIZE_MAX`, causing `memcpy` to write 50 bytes into a 0-byte destination buffer, followed by `buf[50] = '\0'`.

Title: Global Out-of-Bounds Read and Lack of Null Termination in Pull Context URI Copy
Analysis:
- Source: LwM2M Firmware or Software Management Object's static package URI buffer size (`PACKAGE_URI_LEN` = 255) vs the active Pull Context's URI buffer size (`LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN` = `CONFIG_LWM2M_SWMGMT_PACKAGE_URI_LEN` which defaults to 128).
- Sanitization/Validation: When transfer begins, `memcpy(context.uri, uri, LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN)` copies `LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN` bytes from `uri`.
  - Case A (If `LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN` < 255, e.g. 128): If the source URI has length between 128 and 255, the destination string is copied *without a null terminator*. A subsequent `strlen(context.uri)` or `http_parser_parse_url` on it will read beyond `context.uri` bounds (global memory out-of-bounds read).
  - Case B (If `LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN` > 255): `memcpy` will copy more than 255 bytes from the 255-byte global source `uri` buffer, reading adjacent global variables out-of-bounds.
- Sink: `memcpy(context.uri, uri, LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN)` and subsequent `strlen`/`http_parser_parse_url` operations.
- Conceptual Exploit Payload:
  An attacker writes a long package URI (e.g. 150 bytes) to the firmware object.
  Under default configuration, `LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN` is 128.
  `memcpy` copies 128 bytes of the URI without a null-terminator.
  When `http_parser_parse_url` is called, it parses beyond 128 bytes, accessing active fields in `context` (such as `is_firmware_uri`, callbacks, and `firmware_ctx`), leading to information disclosure, memory corruption, or a crash.
